subject: Model improvement exclusion & subprocessor routing — DPA addendum request
messages:
From: Susan Brooks <susan.brooks@orionhealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@orionhealth.com>, Legal <legal@orionhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T17:14:00Z
Subject: Request: model improvement exclusion + subprocessor/evidence pack

Michael / Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and Legal have reviewed the standard DPA and we have two items that are blockers for signature unless clarified in an addendum:

1) Model improvement exclusion: Orion needs explicit, contract-level confirmation that customer-provided inputs (prompts and conversational transcripts) will not be used to improve or retrain any models (both proprietary and third-party models) unless we explicitly opt in via a separate agreement. We cannot accept ambiguous language.

2) Subprocessor and transfer routing: we require a list of subprocessors processing EU customer data and a proposed routing plan that ensures EU-residency for customer data or a clear export mechanism with protective measures. Procurement also wants an operational "evidence pack" to verify implementation.

Attached is our redline (Orion_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf) with suggested language. Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood will sign an addendum with a model-improvement exclusion clause?
- If yes, what evidence will you provide to show the exclusion is enforced (logs, retention policy, KV cache behavior, subprocessor attestations)?
- Timeline for a signed addendum and delivery of the evidence pack?

Procurement needs a plan this week for internal approval. If there are two viable alternatives (hosted with documented controls vs dedicated/on-prem), please lay them out and we can route to the right stakeholders.

Thanks —
Susan Brooks
Head of Procurement, Orion Health Systems

--
Attachment: Orion_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf (pdf, 48 KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Susan Brooks <susan.brooks@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T20:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: model improvement exclusion + subprocessor/evidence pack

Susan —

Appreciate the clear asks and the redline. High level response and next steps below. I'll follow up with a short internal thread to align on the operational artifacts we can provide.

Short answers:
- Redwood can commit to a model-improvement exclusion for customer-provided content when requested and captured in an addendum. We typically phrase this as an explicit "Model Improvement Exclusion" addendum that prevents any customer content from being used to train/improve models under our control or those of our service providers unless the customer opts in.
- Evidence: we can generate an Operational Evidence Pack containing: system configuration snapshots (model flags), subprocessor attestations, token retention policy extract, and a short audit log sample showing disabled learning telemetry.

Options (we propose Orion pick one):
A) Hosted + Controls (faster, self-serve): Redwood will attach an addendum that locks processing config (no model improvement) for Orion's tenant; we will provide the evidence pack and an onshore routing plan for EU data flows using eu-west-1 + encrypted transit. Some subprocessors remain (e.g., S3/GCS for backups) — we will supply attestations.

B) Dedicated / Reserved Capacity or Private deployment (stronger guarantees): We offer dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pools (or Private VPC deployment) where we can enforce residency and subprocessor restrictions more strictly. This requires an implementation window and a commercial amendment.

Practical asks for Orion to help speed signoff:
- Confirm which option you prefer (A or B)
- Confirm the exact scope: all chat logs, prompts, and model inputs for the enterprise account? Or only certain products/environments?

I'll get Legal and Ops to draft addendum language and a one-page evidence checklist by EOD tomorrow. If Procurement confirms timeline constraints, escalate to Marissa for customer ops prioritization.

Cheers,
Michael Grant
Director, Customer Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: mg_response_dpa_notes.txt (plain text, 3 KB)

From: Susan Brooks <susan.brooks@orionhealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@orionhealth.com>, Legal <legal@orionhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: model improvement exclusion + subprocessor/evidence pack

Michael —

Thanks, that helps. Procurement leans to Option A as long as the evidence pack is concrete and delivered before signature. A couple of clarifying items Legal asked us to confirm:

- Scope: We need the exclusion to cover all "customer-provided content" (prompts, chat transcripts, uploaded files, and any derived intermediate logs) generated in production and sandbox environments unless explicitly agreed otherwise.
- Subprocessors: please confirm current subprocessors that may touch EU data and whether you can route Orion's tenant away from US-based analytics/transit processors. For example, can you ensure backups and telemetry for Orion remain in eu-west-1 and provide attestations for HashiCorp Vault / monitoring providers if they are involved?
- Evidence expectations: Our legal team enumerated the pack items we need. Quick list attached inline below — can you respond yes/no and expected delivery time?

Evidence pack (procurement checklist):
- Confirmation of addendum language (pdf)
- Subprocessor inventory with EU-residency mapping (csv/pdf)
- A sanitized audit log sample showing the relevant config flags and absence of learning telemetry (csv)
- Retention policy excerpts and KV cache handling notes (pdf)
- Ops runbook excerpt for tenant routing and fallbacks (pdf)

We can sign a DocuSign addendum if the pack is provided and the language matches the redline. Procurement needs the DocuSign link and a committed delivery date.

Thanks —
Susan

Date: 2026-11-20T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: model improvement exclusion + subprocessor/evidence pack

Susan —

Thanks for the confirmation and the checklist. Below is a concrete delivery plan and what's in scope. If that meets Orion's procurement timetable we'll route the DocuSign link by tomorrow.

Commitment summary (what we'll include in the addendum):
- A Model Improvement Exclusion clause: "Redwood will not use, access, or process Customer-provided Content for the purpose of improving or training machine learning models, including tertiary/third-party models, without Customer's explicit, prior written consent."
- Scope: applies to production and sandbox tenant data (prompts, transcripts, uploaded artifacts, and transient KV/cache data) for the Orion account(s) identified in the addendum.
- Subprocessor routing: Redwood will route processing for the Orion tenant to eu-west-1 and will exclude designated non-EU analytics subprocessors for Orion's tenant where technically feasible. Where a subprocessor cannot be excluded entirely, Redwood will provide attestation and compensating controls.

Operational Evidence Pack (deliverables):
1) Signed addendum PDF (redline accepted) — delivery: by 2026-11-21 18:00 UTC
2) Subprocessor inventory with residency mapping (csv) — delivery: 2026-11-21 18:00 UTC
3) Sanitized audit log sample showing disabled learning flags (csv, sanitized) — delivery: 2026-11-22 18:00 UTC
4) Retention policy excerpts + KV cache handling note (pdf) — delivery: 2026-11-22 18:00 UTC
5) Ops runbook excerpt for tenant routing and fallback plan (pdf) — delivery: 2026-11-22 18:00 UTC

We can also provide an optional short video walkthrough of the tenant routing and evidence pack if you want. For Dedicated/Private deployments we will propose a separate SOW if Orion decides to move to option B.

DocuSign + delivery: once you confirm the scope and that the above timeline works for Procurement, Kimberly and I will route the DocuSign link and the addendum. We'll attach the Operational_Evidence_Pack_v1.zip in the Drive folder and share the link above.

If Procurement needs a legal handshake before the evidence pack is complete, we can provide an interim statement-of-facts memo signed by our CISO for procurement review.

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Customer Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
